title: SCID is managed as a medical emergency with:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: SCID is managed as a medical emergency with:
body.explanation: No T or B lymphocytes.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Rhythm decision. Shockable (VF, pulseless VT) vs non-shockable (asystole, PEA), then 2 minutes of CPR.

title: Why must the AED pads not touch?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Why must the AED pads not touch?
options: It burns the hands of the rescuer
It drains the battery of the device
It reduces the effectiveness of the shock
It stops the device analysing the rhythm
body.explanation: Also dry a wet chest and remove clothing.

title: What causes hyperacute graft rejection?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What causes hyperacute graft rejection?
body.explanation: Minutes to hours, with immediate thrombosis.

title: What is the hallmark of acute mesenteric ischaemia?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the hallmark of acute mesenteric ischaemia?
options: Fever as the first and main sign
Pain out of proportion to examination
body.explanation: Tenderness is minimal early.

title: What should be removed before a pelvic sling?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What should be removed before a pelvic sling?
body.explanation: So objects do not press on the pelvis.

title: The commonest cause of sudden cardiac death in people 35 and under is:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The commonest cause of sudden cardiac death in people 35 and under is:
options: Coronary artery disease in the elderly
body.explanation: Coronary disease dominates in older people.

title: Which marker reflects biliary disease?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which marker reflects biliary disease?
body.explanation: With ALP and bilirubin.

title: How should an infant who is choking be managed?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How should an infant who is choking be managed?
options: Heimlich abdominal thrusts, as for adults
Abdominal thrusts only, with the infant upright
Blind finger sweeps until the object comes out
5 back blows then 5 chest thrusts, head low
body.explanation: Face down on the forearm with the head supported.

title: What should you do if a brief seizure occurs at the onset of collapse?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What should you do if a brief seizure occurs at the onset of collapse?
options: Wait until it stops, then assess breathing
body.explanation: A short seizure-like episode can accompany the onset of cardiac arrest.

title: What compression depth does the lecture recommend for an adult?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What compression depth does the lecture recommend for an adult?
body.explanation: At least 5 cm but not more than 6 cm.

title: What share of acute pancreatitis is due to gallstones or alcohol?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What share of acute pancreatitis is due to gallstones or alcohol?
body.explanation: Gallstones slightly more common.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Helmet removal. One rescuer holds in-line, the other removes the helmet, spreading it over the ears.

title: What is typical pain in acute mesenteric ischaemia?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is typical pain in acute mesenteric ischaemia?
options: Pain out of proportion to exam
body.explanation: Delay in diagnosis can be disastrous.

title: What must be noted after applying a tourniquet?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What must be noted after applying a tourniquet?
body.explanation: Note the time; if over an hour from care, loosen slowly at 60 minutes while pressing.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Innate immunity. First line: epithelial barriers, phagocytes, complement, NK cells and type I interferons.

title: When does trephination improve outcome?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: When does trephination improve outcome?
body.explanation: With falling consciousness, anisocoria or hemiparesis.

title: What share of cardiac output goes to the kidneys?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What share of cardiac output goes to the kidneys?
body.explanation: Renal blood flow is 20 percent of cardiac output.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Hyperactivity. Allergy (type I, IgE, mast cells) and autoimmune disease (SLE, MS).

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Recovery position. On the side, so vomit or blood drains; left side in pregnancy.

title: What stimulates thirst?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What stimulates thirst?
body.explanation: Hypothalamic osmoreceptors, or baroreceptors sensing low pressure.

title: How long should you check for breathing?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How long should you check for breathing?
body.explanation: Look, listen and feel for normal breathing for no more than 10 s.

title: What is applied after rinsing a hydrofluoric acid burn?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is applied after rinsing a hydrofluoric acid burn?
body.explanation: Topical 2.5 percent calcium gluconate gel.

title: Which is a cause of cardiogenic shock?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is a cause of cardiogenic shock?
body.explanation: Also myocarditis, drug toxicity, severe AV block, acute valve insufficiency, septal rupture.

title: Does prerenal AKI damage the parenchyma?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Does prerenal AKI damage the parenchyma?
body.explanation: It reverses quickly; prolonged hypoperfusion can cause acute tubular necrosis.

title: If you are more than an hour from care, after 60 minutes you should:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: If you are more than an hour from care, after 60 minutes you should:
options: Tighten it further to be safe
Cut it off and apply a new one
body.explanation: Retighten if heavy bleeding returns; otherwise leave it loosely in place.

title: Which is NOT one of the three aims of first aid?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is NOT one of the three aims of first aid?
body.explanation: Diagnosis belongs to professional care.

title: What fraction of cardiac output goes to the kidneys?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What fraction of cardiac output goes to the kidneys?
body.explanation: Renal blood flow is about 20% of cardiac output.

title: Why is a neutralising agent avoided on a chemical burn?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Why is a neutralising agent avoided on a chemical burn?
options: It is forbidden by first-aid law
It is too expensive to carry
It stains the skin and hides the burn
The reaction generates heat and worsens the injury
body.explanation: Water dilutes and removes the agent safely.

title: Where does the right AED pad go?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Where does the right AED pad go?
options: Right upper chest below the clavicle
Directly over the middle of the sternum
Right lower abdomen, near the hip
body.explanation: The left pad goes below the left armpit over the lower ribs.

title: Which autoantibodies characterise lupus?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which autoantibodies characterise lupus?
body.explanation: SLE is multisystem: skin, kidneys, joints.

title: Acute mitral regurgitation causes shock that is:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Acute mitral regurgitation causes shock that is:
body.explanation: Mechanical causes also include septal rupture and intracavitary thrombus.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Clinical signs. Mottling, cold extremities, capillary refill over 3 s, altered consciousness, oliguria, tachypnoea, tachycardia, high lactate.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Hypovolaemic shock. Haemorrhage, GI losses, extensive burns, dehydration.

title: How should an amputated finger be transported?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How should an amputated finger be transported?
options: Moist wrap, sealed bag, in ice water
body.explanation: Cold but never frozen.

title: Which cells kill virus-infected cells in innate immunity?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which cells kill virus-infected cells in innate immunity?
body.explanation: With type I interferons that block viral replication.

title: What proportion of cardiovascular deaths are sudden cardiac deaths?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What proportion of cardiovascular deaths are sudden cardiac deaths?
body.explanation: And it is the first manifestation of heart disease in up to half of those cases.

title: Which are secondary causes of immunodeficiency? (choose all)
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which are secondary causes of immunodeficiency? (choose all)
body.explanation: HIV, chemotherapy, steroids, immunosuppressants, diabetes, renal or hepatic failure, haematological cancers.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Pancreatic enzymes. Lipase rises in 4 to 8 h, stays up 8 to 14 days, and is more specific than amylase.

title: Which rhythms are shockable?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which rhythms are shockable?
body.explanation: Shock VF/pVT; for asystole or PEA continue CPR.

title: How wide should a tourniquet be?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How wide should a tourniquet be?
body.explanation: Wide, flat and non-stretch; never wire or rope.

title: When are diuretics indicated in AKI?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: When are diuretics indicated in AKI?
body.explanation: Target urine 0.5 to 1 mL/kg/h; otherwise they may worsen outcomes.

title: Which position suits an unconscious breathing victim?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which position suits an unconscious breathing victim?
body.explanation: On the side so vomit or blood drains; the left side in pregnancy.

title: How do calcineurin inhibitors act?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How do calcineurin inhibitors act?
body.explanation: Cyclosporine, tacrolimus.

title: An awake trauma victim with neck pain refuses to lie flat. You should:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: An awake trauma victim with neck pain refuses to lie flat. You should:
options: Tilt the head back to open the airway
Force them flat onto a spine board
Remove any collar to examine the neck
Let them hold their neck comfortably
body.explanation: Forcing may worsen the injury.

title: A pelvic sling is tightened by:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: A pelvic sling is tightened by:
options: Cross it in front and pull both ends
Twisting a stick placed on a knot
Wrapping it twice around the waist
Tying it behind the patient's back
body.explanation: Secure with a knot, clamp or duct tape.

title: Which is a cause of hypovolaemic shock?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is a cause of hypovolaemic shock?
body.explanation: Haemorrhage, GI losses, burns, dehydration.

title: Which is NOT a sign of reduced regional blood flow in shock?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is NOT a sign of reduced regional blood flow in shock?
body.explanation: Patients are tachypnoeic.

title: Skull trephination improves outcome in:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Skull trephination improves outcome in:
body.explanation: Signs: falling consciousness, anisocoria, hemiparesis.

title: How long does an adaptive response take?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How long does an adaptive response take?
body.explanation: Lymphocytes must proliferate and differentiate.

title: Which are scene hazards? (choose all)
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which are scene hazards? (choose all)
body.explanation: Fire, chemicals, electricity, water, traffic, unstable structures, aggressive people.

title: Anaphylactic shock belongs to which family?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Anaphylactic shock belongs to which family?
body.explanation: With septic, inflammatory and spinal shock.

title: Which adrenal zone makes cortisol?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which adrenal zone makes cortisol?
body.explanation: Glomerulosa aldosterone, fasciculata cortisol, reticularis androgens.

title: What defines SCID?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What defines SCID?
body.explanation: Severe infections in the first months; bone marrow transplant is essential.

title: What does the trauma primary survey include?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What does the trauma primary survey include?
body.explanation: Airway with spine stabilisation, breathing, circulation with haemorrhage control, disability, exposure with hypothermia prevention.

title: What is the commonest cause of sudden cardiac death in young athletes in the USA?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the commonest cause of sudden cardiac death in young athletes in the USA?
options: Commotio cordis from a chest blow
body.explanation: As listed in the lecture's etiologies.

title: A general splinting rule is to immobilise:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: A general splinting rule is to immobilise:
options: The joint above and the joint below
body.explanation: And check neurovascular status before and after.

title: What should you do with an uncooperative trauma patient?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What should you do with an uncooperative trauma patient?
body.explanation: Forcing may worsen an injury; let alert patients hold their neck.

title: What share of circulating blood does the brain receive?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What share of circulating blood does the brain receive?
body.explanation: Despite being 2 to 3% of body mass.

title: Which is a cause of obstructive shock?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is a cause of obstructive shock?
body.explanation: Tamponade, pulmonary embolism, tension pneumothorax.

title: Which islet cells make glucagon?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which islet cells make glucagon?
body.explanation: Beta: insulin. Delta: somatostatin, inhibiting both.

title: Which drug blocks T4 to T3 conversion in thyroid storm?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which drug blocks T4 to T3 conversion in thyroid storm?
body.explanation: Beta-blockade, PTU or methimazole, dexamethasone, iodine, cooling.

title: Why does lactate rise in shock?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Why does lactate rise in shock?
options: Cellular hypoxia shifts metabolism to anaerobic pathways
The liver overproduces lactate in shock
Oxygen delivery to the tissues is too high
Renal failure alone blocks lactate excretion
body.explanation: Leading to metabolic acidosis.

title: Before applying a pelvic sling you should:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Before applying a pelvic sling you should:
options: Apply a tourniquet to both legs
body.explanation: So the sling does not press objects against the pelvis.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Recognise. Unresponsive with absent or abnormal (agonal) breathing: assume cardiac arrest.

title: Which is the best test for suspected choledocholithiasis?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is the best test for suspected choledocholithiasis?
body.explanation: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography.

title: What are the four types of shock?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What are the four types of shock?
options: Mild, moderate, severe, critical and fatal
body.explanation: The four broad categories.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Adrenal crisis. Acute severe adrenal insufficiency; classic sign refractory hypotension.

title: What is shock?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is shock?
body.explanation: Widespread failure to oxygenate and nourish the body; a transition between life and death.

title: Which catecholamine is listed for its positive inotropic effect?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which catecholamine is listed for its positive inotropic effect?
body.explanation: With adrenaline and noradrenaline.

title: Which is NOT a listed precipitant of thyroid storm?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is NOT a listed precipitant of thyroid storm?
body.explanation: Also surgery, ACS, stroke, neck trauma, hormone ingestion.

title: The Monro-Kellie doctrine states that:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The Monro-Kellie doctrine states that:
options: The cranium is a fixed volume of brain, blood and CSF
The skull expands to absorb raised pressure
CSF is not produced once adulthood is reached
ICP has no effect on cerebral perfusion
body.explanation: Lowering ICP requires reducing one component.

title: Which is NOT a hormone produced or activated by the kidney?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is NOT a hormone produced or activated by the kidney?
body.explanation: Insulin comes from pancreatic beta cells.

title: Which are immediate complications of AKI? (choose all)
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which are immediate complications of AKI? (choose all)
body.explanation: Pulmonary oedema, hyperkalaemia, hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, metabolic acidosis, uraemia.

title: What most often causes sudden cardiac arrest?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What most often causes sudden cardiac arrest?
body.explanation: Mostly VF or pulseless VT; sometimes PEA or asystole.

title: How is an amputated part preserved?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How is an amputated part preserved?
body.explanation: Moist sterile dressing, watertight bag, inside a bag of ice or ice-water; never freeze.

title: What is the risk of prolonged cooling of a large burn?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the risk of prolonged cooling of a large burn?
body.explanation: Cooling under 10% TBSA can be continued longer for pain.

title: How is an improvised tourniquet tightened?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How is an improvised tourniquet tightened?
options: By twisting a stick placed on the knot
body.explanation: Then tie or tape the stick so it does not unwind.

title: What does hypothermia do to ICP?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What does hypothermia do to ICP?
body.explanation: Lower temperature decreases cerebral blood flow, ICP and metabolism.

title: Which is an indication for renal replacement therapy?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is an indication for renal replacement therapy?
body.explanation: Also refractory overload and severe electrolyte or acid-base disorders.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Splinting. Immobilise the joint above and below; check neurovascular status before and after.

title: Over what CPP range is cerebral blood flow autoregulated?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Over what CPP range is cerebral blood flow autoregulated?
body.explanation: Below 60 ischaemia; above 160 hypertensive encephalopathy.

title: What breathing pattern suggests DKA?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What breathing pattern suggests DKA?
body.explanation: Deep breathing compensating for acidosis.

title: What is the compression rate?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the compression rate?
body.explanation: With minimal interruptions and full recoil.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Obstructive shock. Tamponade, pulmonary embolism, tension pneumothorax.

title: What is the definitive treatment of a space-occupying lesion?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the definitive treatment of a space-occupying lesion?
body.explanation: Operative drainage of blood and CSF.

title: Which lab pattern fits adrenal crisis?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which lab pattern fits adrenal crisis?
options: Low Na, high K, low glucose
High Na, low K, high glucose
Low Na, low K, high glucose
body.explanation: Aldosterone and cortisol deficiency.

title: What are the three Cs of emergency care?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What are the three Cs of emergency care?
body.explanation: Check the victim, call EMS, care for the victim.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Burns. Stop the burning process, remove jewellery, cool with water for about 30 minutes.

title: Which precipitate thyroid storm? (choose all)
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which precipitate thyroid storm? (choose all)
body.explanation: Infection, surgery, ACS, stroke, trauma, noncompliance, thyroid hormone ingestion, iodine contrast.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Protect and call. Gloves, then call the EMS.

title: Which are parameters of hepatic synthesis? (choose all)
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which are parameters of hepatic synthesis? (choose all)
body.explanation: Albumin, cholinesterase and prothrombin time.

title: A vehicle involved in a crash is lying on its side. What should you do?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: A vehicle involved in a crash is lying on its side. What should you do?
options: Right it quickly so the victims can climb out
Push it off the road to clear the traffic
Start its engine to move it somewhere safer
Not try to right it, and stabilise it only if safe and trained
body.explanation: Righting it is dangerous; block or rope it only if safe and trained.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Cerebral perfusion pressure. CPP = MAP - ICP; autoregulated between 60 and 160 mmHg.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Vicious circle. Low CPP causes ischaemia, which causes more swelling and higher ICP.

title: Which prophylaxis does the lecture cite for HIV patients?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which prophylaxis does the lecture cite for HIV patients?
body.explanation: Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis is cited as part of infection prevention in secondary immunodeficiency.
option_notes: Not cited for HIV in the lecture.
An antacid, not an anti-infective prophylaxis.
Cited in the lecture for HIV prophylaxis.
Not cited in the lecture.

title: Above what blood loss may shock occur?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Above what blood loss may shock occur?
body.explanation: Loss of over 25 percent of blood volume can cause shock.

title: What is the commonest cause of AKI?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the commonest cause of AKI?
body.explanation: 40 to 55 percent of cases, from kidney hypoperfusion.

title: What does glucagon do?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What does glucagon do?
body.explanation: Gluconeogenesis, glycogenolysis, beta-oxidation; inhibits glycolysis.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: True tests of liver function. Prothrombin time and albumin reflect synthetic function.

title: What mediates type I hypersensitivity?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What mediates type I hypersensitivity?
body.explanation: Sensitisation, then mast cell degranulation with histamine and leukotrienes.

title: When should cervical spine injury be suspected?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: When should cervical spine injury be suspected?
options: Fall or dive from a height
body.explanation: Also crush injuries, road and sports accidents.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Distributive shock. Sepsis, anaphylaxis, inflammatory states, spinal shock.

title: Tacrolimus belongs to which class?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Tacrolimus belongs to which class?
body.explanation: Like ciclosporin; blocks T-cell activation.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Alert. Call the emergency services at once and get an AED.

title: What is the commonest cause of secondary insufficiency?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the commonest cause of secondary insufficiency?
body.explanation: It suppresses ACTH.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Acute mesenteric ischaemia. Pain out of proportion to examination; CT angiography first.

title: How should white phosphorus on the skin be managed?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How should white phosphorus on the skin be managed?
body.explanation: It ignites on contact with air.

title: What is the first step to stop external bleeding?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the first step to stop external bleeding?
body.explanation: Protect yourself, apply a dressing and press; wound packing for deep wounds.

title: Which does NOT transiently raise ICP?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which does NOT transiently raise ICP?
body.explanation: Movement, position, pain, fever, coughing and straining raise ICP transiently.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Spinal motion restriction. Manual in-line stabilisation of the head and neck when a spinal injury is suspected.

title: How is the airway opened in a non-trauma victim?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How is the airway opened in a non-trauma victim?
body.explanation: Head tilt-chin lift; jaw thrust if cervical injury is suspected.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Hepatic blood supply. The liver gets 25% of cardiac output; the portal vein gives 75% of flow but 50% of oxygen.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Vaccination. Safe exposure to antigen creates memory; boosters when immunity wanes or the pathogen changes.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Wound packing. Fill deep wounds with gauze to press on the bleeding source.

title: Which drug blocks peripheral T4 to T3 conversion in thyroid storm?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which drug blocks peripheral T4 to T3 conversion in thyroid storm?
body.explanation: PTU and methimazole block synthesis; iodine blocks release.

title: Hypothermia lowers ICP by:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Hypothermia lowers ICP by:
options: Increasing CSF production by the plexus
body.explanation: Lower temperatures reduce CBF, ICP and metabolism.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Open the airway. Head tilt with chin lift, or jaw thrust if trauma is suspected.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Call the emergency services. Dial 15 in Morocco and give the exact location.

title: How long should a chemical burn be rinsed at least?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How long should a chemical burn be rinsed at least?
body.explanation: With large amounts of water; no neutralising agent.

title: Extensive burns cause which shock types?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Extensive burns cause which shock types?
options: Neither: burns do not cause shock
body.explanation: Burns appear in both lists in the lecture.

title: The Fick equation states that VO2 equals:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The Fick equation states that VO2 equals:
body.explanation: Used to measure cardiac output.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Rescue breaths. 30:2 if trained; otherwise continuous compressions.

title: Normal GFR in adult men is about:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Normal GFR in adult men is about:
body.explanation: About 120 in women; about 180 L/day.

title: How many back blows does the lecture give for an adult choking victim?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How many back blows does the lecture give for an adult choking victim?
body.explanation: Rapid, sharp blows between the shoulder blades.

title: What is the compression-to-breath ratio?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the compression-to-breath ratio?

They must wait for a fever to develop first
They depend on complement being consumed first

It lies between two resistance arterioles

title: First-line treatment of anaphylaxis is:

Apply a dressing and direct pressure

title: What is personal protective equipment for?

Protecting the rescuer against specific hazards
Calling the EMS from the scene

title: Which element is at the arrow?

title: How do you relieve choking in a pregnant woman?

title: Why must a helmet be spread laterally during removal?

options: It is egg-shaped and must clear the ears
To remove the victim's glasses first
To protect the chin from the strap
To open the visor for the airway

title: Why are booster doses needed?
subject: subj:firstaid

A booster is needed to cause mild disease
Immunity wanes or the pathogen evolves
Memory cells must be stopped regularly

title: Which element is at the arrow?

title: A palpable radial pulse suggests a systolic pressure of at least about:

title: What share of overall mortality in industrialised nations is sudden cardiac death?
subject: subj:firstaid

Correct: 15 to 20% of all deaths.

subject: subj:firstaid

body.explanation: Health professionals check the pulse for no more than 10 seconds; if no definite pulse, presume arrest and start CPR.

title: Which imaging is first-line for acute mesenteric ischaemia?

Colonic watershed areas prone to ischaemia

The patient is over 70 years old
The stone is larger than 1 cm

Defibrillation: attach the AED at once

The trachea collapses under its weight
The epiglottis ruptures and blocks it
The tongue falls back into the pharynx

Only the head and the scalp

To the side of the neck, over the carotid
To the centre of the chest (breastbone)
Between the shoulder blades, on the back

body.explanation: The arrow points to: Pelvic sling. Centred on the greater trochanters, crossed in front and tightened.

title: SOFT stands for:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: SOFT stands for:
body.explanation: The CAT is the Combat Application Tourniquet.

title: Which is NOT a determinant of stroke volume?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is NOT a determinant of stroke volume?
body.explanation: SV depends on preload, inotropy and afterload.

title: Which marker reflects biliary disease?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which marker reflects biliary disease?
body.explanation: GGT, ALP and bilirubin.

title: How long should the breathing check last at most?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How long should the breathing check last at most?
body.explanation: Look, listen and feel for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds.

title: Primary adrenal insufficiency becomes evident when about how much adrenal function is lost?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Primary adrenal insufficiency becomes evident when about how much adrenal function is lost?
body.explanation: Both cortisol and aldosterone then fail.

title: Where is a tourniquet placed?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Where is a tourniquet placed?
options: As close above the wound as possible
At the root of the limb always
body.explanation: Between the wound and the heart, close to the wound.

title: Should a motorcycle helmet be removed prehospital?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Should a motorcycle helmet be removed prehospital?
body.explanation: Full-face helmets block airway care; remove with in-line stabilisation.

title: What is the antidote for paracetamol hepatotoxicity?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the antidote for paracetamol hepatotoxicity?
body.explanation: Given to all at risk with any liver injury.

title: Which cells provide innate defence against virus-infected cells?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which cells provide innate defence against virus-infected cells?
body.explanation: Together with type I interferons.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Amputated part. Wrapped in moist dressing, bagged, then placed in ice water, never frozen.

title: Which cells kill tumour cells presenting antigen on MHC I?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which cells kill tumour cells presenting antigen on MHC I?
body.explanation: NK cells detect absent MHC I.

title: What is normal ICP in healthy adults?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is normal ICP in healthy adults?
body.explanation: Transient rises occur with movement, pain, fever, coughing and straining.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Hypothalamus and pituitary. The hypothalamus leads the endocrine system through the anterior and posterior pituitary.

title: Which cells release renin?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which cells release renin?
body.explanation: In response to low perfusion, sympathetic tone or low NaCl at the macula densa (NKCC2).

title: What is the antidote for paracetamol toxicity?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the antidote for paracetamol toxicity?
body.explanation: For anyone at risk with ingestion and liver injury; transplant if severe.

title: From what ICP is it considered raised?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: From what ICP is it considered raised?
body.explanation: The take-home message defines raised ICP as 20 mmHg or more.

title: What is the commonest primary immunodeficiency?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the commonest primary immunodeficiency?
body.explanation: Recurrent ENT and GI infections, often asymptomatic.

title: Cerebral perfusion pressure equals:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Cerebral perfusion pressure equals:
body.explanation: A rise in ICP lowers CPP.

title: Autoregulation keeps cerebral blood flow constant for CPP between:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Autoregulation keeps cerebral blood flow constant for CPP between:
body.explanation: Outside that range CBF follows CPP linearly.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Management. Supportive care, then NAC for paracetamol, revascularisation or resection, ERCP for biliary obstruction.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Primary survey. Airway with C-spine, Breathing, Circulation with haemorrhage control, Disability, Exposure without hypothermia.

title: Which drug is listed as able to precipitate acute adrenal insufficiency?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which drug is listed as able to precipitate acute adrenal insufficiency?
body.explanation: With ketoconazole and steroid withdrawal.

title: How long should a chemical burn be rinsed?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How long should a chemical burn be rinsed?
body.explanation: Large amounts of water; never neutralise, which produces heat.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Assess severity. Where, arterial or venous, and whether more than 25% of blood volume is lost (shock).

title: Where does ADH-dependent water reabsorption occur?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Where does ADH-dependent water reabsorption occur?
body.explanation: It sets final urine concentration; urine is about 1 percent of filtrate.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Thyroid storm. Life-threatening thyrotoxicosis with fever, tachycardia and CNS dysfunction.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Acute pancreatitis. 80% from gallstones or alcohol; autodigestion of the gland.

title: How long is CPR continued between rhythm checks?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How long is CPR continued between rhythm checks?
body.explanation: CPR 2 minutes, then reassess the rhythm.

title: What must you check besides external bleeding?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What must you check besides external bleeding?
body.explanation: Consider internal and external, arterial or venous bleeding.

title: What are the three aims of first aid?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What are the three aims of first aid?
body.explanation: First aid is immediate care before professional help arrives.

title: Which is an absolute contraindication to helmet removal?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is an absolute contraindication to helmet removal?
options: Neck pain or paraesthesia during removal
The helmet has a full-face guard
body.explanation: Also an impaled object through the helmet.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Juxtaglomerular apparatus. Low NaCl at the macula densa or low perfusion triggers renin release.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Diabetic ketoacidosis. Insulin lack: hyperglycaemia, ketones and acidosis.

title: According to the lecture, amylase may be normal in pancreatitis caused by:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: According to the lecture, amylase may be normal in pancreatitis caused by:
body.explanation: The lecture cites hypertriglyceridaemia as a cause of pancreatitis with normal amylase; lipase is more sensitive and specific.
option_notes: Can mask the amylase rise; cited in the lecture.
Amylase usually rises.
Amylase usually rises markedly in gallstone pancreatitis.
Post-ERCP pancreatitis shows a raised amylase.

title: Which is the commonest cause of intrinsic AKI?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is the commonest cause of intrinsic AKI?
options: Vasculitis of the small renal vessels
Ischaemic or septic acute tubular necrosis
body.explanation: Nephrotoxins and allergic nephritis are other causes.

title: Why are cells 'starving' in DKA despite high glucose?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Why are cells 'starving' in DKA despite high glucose?
options: Glucose is destroyed in the blood
Without insulin, glucose cannot enter cells
body.explanation: So fatty acids are burned into ketones.

title: What is the commonest cause of postrenal AKI?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the commonest cause of postrenal AKI?
body.explanation: Prostatic disease, anticholinergics, neurogenic bladder.

title: What is the commonest cause in the elderly?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the commonest cause in the elderly?
body.explanation: In the young: channelopathies and cardiomyopathies; in young athletes: HCM and anomalous coronaries.

title: What causes 80 percent of acute pancreatitis?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What causes 80 percent of acute pancreatitis?
body.explanation: Gallstones slightly more common.

title: What is the formula for mean arterial pressure?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the formula for mean arterial pressure?
body.explanation: MAP = CO x SVR = SV x HR x SVR.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Thyroid storm treatment. Fluids, cooling, beta-blockade, PTU or methimazole, dexamethasone, iodine.

title: The CT sign of hydrocephalus in the lecture is:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: The CT sign of hydrocephalus in the lecture is:
options: Midline shift from a large haematoma
A linear skull fracture on bone windows
Air in the ventricles after trauma
Ventricular enlargement with effaced peripheral sulci
body.explanation: Managed with CSF shunts.

title: How long does lipase stay raised after acute pancreatitis?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How long does lipase stay raised after acute pancreatitis?
body.explanation: Amylase normalises in 3 to 5 days.

title: What does splinting immobilise?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What does splinting immobilise?
body.explanation: Check neurovascular status before and after, cover open wounds.

title: Which breathing is a sign of cardiac arrest?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which breathing is a sign of cardiac arrest?
body.explanation: Slow, irregular gasping means cardiac arrest.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Secure the scene. Look before rushing in, remove dangers, protect yourself with PPE.

title: Which structure leads the endocrine system?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which structure leads the endocrine system?
body.explanation: The hypothalamus directs the pituitary and downstream glands.

title: What should you do if in doubt about arrest?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What should you do if in doubt about arrest?
body.explanation: Unresponsive with abnormal breathing means cardiac arrest.

title: How does HIV cause immunodeficiency?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How does HIV cause immunodeficiency?
body.explanation: Collapse of adaptive immunity; cotrimoxazole prophylaxis.

title: Which imaging suits suspected choledocholithiasis?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which imaging suits suspected choledocholithiasis?
body.explanation: Ultrasound for gallstones, CT for obstruction and ischaemia, EUS for pancreatic cancer.

title: Which pancreatic enzyme is more specific?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which pancreatic enzyme is more specific?
body.explanation: Lipase rises at 4 to 8 h, lasts 8 to 14 days, and is more sensitive and specific.

title: Which material must never be used as a tourniquet?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which material must never be used as a tourniquet?
body.explanation: Narrow materials cut the skin and crush tissue.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Normal GFR. About 120 (women) to 130 (men) mL/min/1.73 m², about 180 L/day.

title: Atopy is:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Atopy is:
options: A tendency to produce IgE to low-dose allergens
An autoimmune attack on the patient's own tissues
A type of graft rejection mediated by T cells
A primary immunodeficiency affecting B cells
body.explanation: With asthma, eczema or dermatitis.

title: What is primary adrenal insufficiency called?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is primary adrenal insufficiency called?
body.explanation: About 90 percent of adrenal function lost; no cortisol or aldosterone.

title: What must a first responder do before acting?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What must a first responder do before acting?
body.explanation: Stay calm, act within your training, call for help, and secure the scene first.

title: Which burn needs calcium gluconate gel after irrigation?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which burn needs calcium gluconate gel after irrigation?
body.explanation: Calcium binds the fluoride ion.

title: Which is an acute cause of adrenal insufficiency listed in the lecture?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is an acute cause of adrenal insufficiency listed in the lecture?
body.explanation: Postpartum pituitary necrosis.

title: What determines stroke volume?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What determines stroke volume?
body.explanation: The three determinants of SV.

title: Kussmaul breathing in DKA is:
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Kussmaul breathing in DKA is:
options: Deep breathing with a fruity odour
body.explanation: Respiratory compensation for metabolic acidosis.

title: What does the Fick equation give?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What does the Fick equation give?
body.explanation: Oxygen consumption from cardiac output and the arteriovenous oxygen difference.

title: When does amylase return to normal?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: When does amylase return to normal?
body.explanation: Short half-life; it may be normal in hypertriglyceridaemic pancreatitis.

title: When are diuretics indicated in AKI?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: When are diuretics indicated in AKI?
body.explanation: Target urine output 0.5 to 1 mL/kg/h.

title: What is normal GFR in adult men?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is normal GFR in adult men?
body.explanation: About 120 in women, 130 in men, 180 L/day; falls about 1 mL/min/year after 40.

title: What should you do if you cannot or will not give rescue breaths?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What should you do if you cannot or will not give rescue breaths?
options: Use the AED and do nothing else
Wait for EMS without touching the victim
body.explanation: Compression-only CPR still circulates oxygenated blood.

title: How do tumours escape CD8+ T cells?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: How do tumours escape CD8+ T cells?
options: By losing or altering MHC class I
body.explanation: Also inhibitory molecules, suppressive cytokines, Tregs, M2 macrophages.

title: Which airway manoeuvre is preferred when trauma to the neck is suspected?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which airway manoeuvre is preferred when trauma to the neck is suspected?
body.explanation: The jaw thrust opens the airway with less neck movement.

title: What is the first imaging for mesenteric ischaemia?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the first imaging for mesenteric ischaemia?
body.explanation: It shows the arterial occlusion and thickened bowel.

title: What does ABCDE stand for?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What does ABCDE stand for?
options: Airway, Blood, Cardiac, Drugs, Eyes, Ears
Alert, Bleed, Cool, Dress, Evacuate, Exit
Assess, Bandage, Call, Drive, Exit, Escort
body.explanation: The primary survey identifies life threats.

title: Which transiently raise ICP? (choose all)
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which transiently raise ICP? (choose all)
body.explanation: Movement, position, pain, fever, coughing and straining.

title: What is the normal ICP in healthy adults?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: What is the normal ICP in healthy adults?
body.explanation: Raised ICP is 20 mmHg or more.

title: Which is the commonest cause of AKI?
subject: subj:firstaid

body.stem: Which is the commonest cause of AKI?
body.explanation: 40 to 55% of cases.
